faqs.a: Each real-world asset is represented by an ERC-3643 security token. When you invest, you receive tokens in proportion to your USDC contribution, and only wallets with a verified identity can hold or receive them.
When a project distributes dividends, the platform publishes the distribution on-chain with a Merkle proof. We let you know and you claim it in USDC from My holdings, straight to your wallet.

faqs.q: How can I sell my tokens?
faqs.a: The secondary market between investors is in development. If an asset is liquidated, you claim your capital from My holdings at the liquidation price.

It's the identity verification required by anti-money-laundering rules. You fill in your details under Profile → KYC, the team reviews them and, once approved, we register your identity on-chain to enable your investments.
One token. The price of each token is shown on each project's page, along with the amount available.

faqs.q: What are the risks of investing?
faqs.a: Any investment in real-world assets can lose value, and estimated returns are not guaranteed. Review each project's documents before investing, and diversify.
BRIK is Brikme's utility token. Its presale hasn't opened yet; the planned benefits are fee discounts, early access to projects and participation in governance.
Not while the platform is in its test environment: the USDC and POL are test tokens with no value. You can request test funds from My holdings.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.lead: The new words you'll come across in Brikme, explained without jargon.

welcome.title: Welcome to Brikme
welcome.summary: What Brikme is, your wallet, USDC, KYC and where to see your investments.

intro.title: Welcome to Brikme
intro.body: Here you can invest in real-world assets (real estate, farmland, energy) by buying small shares called tokens. In a minute we'll show you the basics.

wallet.title: Your wallet: your account and your purse
wallet.body: Your wallet lets you sign in to Brikme without a password, and it's where you keep your money and your tokens. Nobody else can move them: you authorize every transaction with a signature.

usdc.title: USDC, the digital dollar
usdc.body: You invest and get paid in USDC: each USDC is worth 1 US dollar, 1 to 1. You deposit it into your wallet from My Holdings.

kyc.title: Verify your identity (KYC)
kyc.body: Before you invest, we ask you to verify who you are. It's required by law for real-world assets and protects everyone from fraud. You do it just once from your Profile.

holdings.title: Where to see your investments
holdings.body: In My Holdings you'll see your balance, your tokens, dividends to claim and all your transactions.

help.title: Help whenever you need it
help.body: Every section has a “How does it work?” button to review its guide. The Help Center has all the guides and a glossary of new terms.

feed.title: Feed
feed.summary: Company updates, milestones, following, commenting and filtering.

news.title: Company updates
news.body: Here you'll see what the companies behind each project post: progress, results and announcements. Posts marked “Milestone” are major achievements.

follow.title: Follow companies
follow.body: Tap “Follow” on a company so you never miss its updates or upcoming projects.

comment.title: Comment and ask
comment.body: You can like and comment. It's a great way to ask the company about its project before investing.

filter.title: Filter what interests you
filter.body: Search by company or project and filter by post type to see only what matters to you.

project.title: From post to project
project.body: “View project” takes you to the full project page to review the numbers and, if you like, invest.

tokenizations.title: Tokenizations
tokenizations.summary: What tokenizing means, what a token is, estimated APY and % funded.

what.title: What does tokenizing an asset mean?
what.body: It means dividing a real-world asset (a building, a farm, a solar plant) into many digital shares called tokens. That way you can invest with little money, and your share is recorded on the blockchain.

card.title: Each card is a project
card.body: A token represents a share of the asset and entitles you to your share of its returns. Tap the card to see the full project page.

apy.title: Estimated APY
apy.body: It's the estimated annual return: how much your investment could earn in a year. It's a projection, not a guarantee.

funded.title: % funded
funded.body: Shows how much of the issuance other investors have already bought. When it reaches 100%, the initial sale closes.

filter.title: Filter and compare
filter.body: Filter by asset type or return to find projects that suit you.

project.title: Project page
project.summary: Price per token, estimated return, documents, how to invest and risks.
project.where: Shown when you open a project.

intro.title: The project page
intro.body: Everything you need to decide is here: what the asset is, who manages it, how much it could return and its documents.

price.title: Price per token
price.body: It's what each share of the asset costs, in USDC (1 USDC = 1 dollar). You can start with a single token.

apy.title: Estimated return (APY)
apy.body: It's an estimate of how much it could return in a year. It isn't guaranteed: it depends on how the asset performs.

funded.title: Funding progress
funded.body: The percentage of tokens already sold. Once it reaches 100%, tokens can only be bought on the secondary market.

docs.title: Documents and updates
docs.body: These tabs hold the token structure, the legal documents and the company's updates. Read them before investing.

invest.title: How to invest
invest.body: Choose how many tokens you want, tap Invest and confirm in your wallet. You need a verified identity and USDC in your balance.

risks.title: Keep the risks in mind
risks.body: Every investment carries risk: the asset may return less than estimated, and selling your tokens may take time. Only invest what you can hold.

checkout.title: Checkout
checkout.summary: Why your wallet asks for two signatures, what gas is and what happens next.
checkout.where: Shown when you invest in a project.

review.title: Review your purchase
review.body: Here you'll see how many tokens you're buying, the price and the total in USDC before you pay.

signatures.title: Your wallet will ask for two signatures
signatures.body: First you authorize the exact USDC amount for this purchase, not a cent more. Then you confirm the transaction.

gas.title: What is gas?
gas.body: Every blockchain transaction pays a small network fee, called gas. Brikme doesn't charge it: your wallet shows you the amount before you confirm.

after.title: What happens next?
after.body: Once the network confirms, the tokens arrive in your wallet and you'll see them in My Holdings, where you also claim your dividends.

secondary.title: Secondary market
secondary.summary: Buying and selling between investors, discount or premium, fees and offers.

intro.title: Buying and selling between investors
intro.body: Here investors buy and sell tokens with each other after the issuance. Every trade happens directly between wallets.

price.title: Asking price vs. real price
price.body: Each offer shows the seller's asking price and the token's reference value. If they ask less, it's a discount; if they ask more, a premium.

buy.title: Buy
buy.body: Your wallet approves the exact USDC amount and confirms the purchase. The tokens go straight to your wallet.

sell.title: Sell your tokens
sell.body: List a sale by choosing the amount and price. When it sells, the seller's fee is deducted, and you'll see it before confirming.

withdraw.title: Your tokens stay in your wallet
withdraw.body: Listing a sale doesn't take the tokens out of your wallet: they only move when someone buys. You can withdraw your offer whenever you like.

holdings.title: My Holdings
holdings.summary: USDC balance, deposits, withdrawals, dividends, capital and transactions.

balance.title: Your USDC balance
balance.body: It's the money available in your wallet to invest, in digital dollars (1 USDC = 1 dollar).

deposit.title: Deposit
deposit.body: We show you your wallet address and the network. Send USDC only over that network: if you use another one, the funds may be lost.

testFunds.title: Test funds
testFunds.body: We're on a test network: under Deposit you'll find “Test funds” to practice with play money. They don't exist on the real network.

withdraw.title: Withdraw
withdraw.body: Send your USDC to another wallet or to an exchange. Double-check the address: blockchain transfers can't be reversed.

dividends.title: Dividends
dividends.body: When a project distributes profits, you get a share based on your tokens. It appears as “to claim” and you claim it in USDC from your investments.

capital.title: Capital after liquidation
capital.body: When a project ends and is liquidated, you get back your share of the capital with “Claim capital”.

movements.title: Transactions
movements.body: Your history: deposits, investments, dividends and withdrawals, each one recorded on the blockchain.

token.title: BRIK token
token.summary: What the platform token is, its sale rounds and its utilities.

intro.title: BRIK, the platform token
intro.body: BRIK is a utility token: it doesn't represent a real-world asset, but benefits within Brikme.

sale.title: Sale rounds
sale.body: It's sold in rounds, each with its own price and allocation. The bar shows how much of the current round has been sold.

utilities.title: What is it for?
utilities.body: Here are its utilities within the platform. Read them before buying: its value can go up or down.

buy.title: Buy BRIK
buy.body: When the sale is open, you'll be able to buy from here with USDC, confirming in your wallet.

position.title: Your position
position.body: Here you'll see how many BRIK you hold in your wallet.

profile.title: Profile
profile.summary: Identity verification (KYC), on-chain identity, privacy and your company.

intro.title: Your profile
intro.body: This is where you manage your account: details, identity verification, documents, privacy and your company.

kyc.title: Identity verification (KYC)
kyc.body: Fill in your details just once under “Account and security”. Once approved, your wallet receives an on-chain identity: a seal that says “verified” without publishing your data.

privacy.title: Your privacy
privacy.body: Your personal data is never published on the blockchain. Under Privacy you choose whether other investors can see your name, your photo or which projects you invested in (never the amounts).

company.title: Your company
company.body: If you want to tokenize an asset, register your company here. We verify it (KYB) before it can publish projects.

tokenize.title: Tokenize an asset
tokenize.summary: How to request the tokenization of an asset and the status of your application.

intro.title: Tokenize your asset
intro.body: If your company has an income-generating asset, you can finance it by selling tokens to investors. It all starts with an application.

steps.title: A step-by-step application
steps.body: Asset type, information, token structure, contact and review. Add documents that back the asset: they speed up the review.

status.title: Track the status
status.body: In “My applications” you'll see where each one stands: submitted, under review, approved or rejected. If anything is missing, we'll let you know.

after.title: After approval
after.body: Our team structures the token together with you and publishes the project in Tokenizations so investors can buy.

companies.title: Companies
companies.summary: Company profiles, verification, following and how to register yours.
companies.where: Shown when you open a company's profile.

intro.title: Company profile
intro.body: Each company posts its projects and progress here. Check who's behind it before investing.

verified.title: Verified company
verified.body: This badge means Brikme reviewed its legal documents (KYB, the company verification).

follow.title: Follow it
follow.body: When you follow a company, you see its updates in your feed and hear about its new projects.

tabs.title: Projects, milestones and reviews
tabs.body: Browse the tabs to see its projects, the milestones it has reached and what other investors think.

own.title: Do you have a company?
own.body: Register it from your Profile, under “Register my company”. Once it's verified, you can apply to tokenize an asset.

blockchain.definition: A public, shared ledger that nobody can secretly delete or change. It records who holds each token and every transaction, so anyone can verify it.

wallet.definition: It's your account and your purse at the same time: you use it to sign in to Brikme (no password) and to keep your USDC and your tokens. Only you can authorize transactions from your wallet.

direccion.definition: Your wallet's "account number": a code that starts with 0x. Share it to receive funds; never share your secret phrase or your private key.

firma.definition: It's how you say "yes, I authorize this" from your wallet. A signature to sign in costs nothing; a signature that moves money becomes a transaction.

usdc.definition: A digital dollar: each USDC is worth 1 US dollar and is backed 1 to 1. It's the currency you invest with and receive dividends in on Brikme.

token.definition: A digital unit that represents a share of a real-world asset (for example, a fraction of a property or a harvest). Holding tokens entitles you to a proportional share of its returns.

tokenizacion.definition: Dividing a real-world asset into many tokens so several people can invest in it with small amounts. Ownership of each token is recorded on the blockchain.

contrato.definition: A program that lives on the blockchain and enforces rules automatically, without intermediaries: for example, delivering your tokens when you pay or distributing dividends among investors.

red.definition: The blockchain where transactions are recorded. On a test network the money is play money: it's for practicing without risk and has no real value.

gas.definition: A small fee the network charges to record a transaction. Brikme doesn't charge it; your wallet shows you the amount before you confirm.

kyc.definition: KYC ("know your customer") means verifying who you are; KYB is the same for companies. The law requires it to invest in real-world assets, and it protects everyone from fraud.

identidad.definition: A seal on the blockchain that says "this wallet is verified", without publishing your personal data. It's what lets your wallet receive tokens of regulated assets.

pool.definition: Each project's fund: it gathers investors' money, delivers the tokens and then distributes the returns and the capital.

apy.definition: How much your investment could return in a year, as a percentage. It's the project's estimate, not a promise: the actual result may be higher or lower.

dividendo.definition: Your share of the asset's profits based on your tokens. It's paid in USDC and you claim it from My Holdings.

liquidacion.definition: The closing of a project: the asset is sold or its term ends, and the capital is distributed among investors according to their tokens.

primario.definition: Where you buy tokens directly from the project when it raises funds (Tokenizations).

secundario.definition: Where investors buy and sell tokens with each other after the issuance. The seller sets the price.

faucet.definition: A tap of play money for practicing on the test network. It never exists on the real network.
